_meta.description: Optional MCPs (NOT loaded by default). Run `/setup-mcp` to activate any of these. Activation patches `opencode.json` and restarts opencode to take effect.
_meta.rationale: 100% value when needed, 0% cost (no boot slowdown, no leaked tokens) when not. `playwright` moved here from opencode.json on 2026-08-12 (token consumption opt-in). `context7` stays default-active (library docs, no secrets) and is therefore NOT listed here. Every other MCP is user-triggered. This file is only read by `node .opencode/bin/setup-mcp.js` (manual command); opencode itself never parses it.

optional_mcps.name: playwright
optional_mcps.description: Browser automation for E2E tests and web scraping (Playwright MCP). Previously loaded by default; moved to opt-in on 2026-08-12 to cut boot tokens.
optional_mcps.use_when: Running E2E tests, browser workflows, scraping, or visual checks.

optional_mcps.name: github
optional_mcps.description: Read GitHub issues, PRs, code search, repo metadata directly from the agent. Replaces manual `gh` CLI invocations with structured MCP tools (list_issues, get_pull_request, search_code, etc).

GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.description: GitHub PAT. Needs 'repo' scope for full read, plus 'read:org' if working with org repos. Generate at https://github.com/settings/tokens (fine-grained token recommended).

optional_mcps.use_when: Reviewing PRs that need GitHub context, fetching issues, code search across the org, automating release notes from merged PRs.

optional_mcps.name: postgres
optional_mcps.description: Read-only SQL queries against a PostgreSQL database. Useful for debugging production issues, validating schema, running ad-hoc analytics. By default the connection is read-only (separate role recommended).

POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING.description: PostgreSQL connection string. Format: postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=require. RECOMMEND a read-only role for safety.

optional_mcps.use_when: Investigating data issues, validating migrations, debugging ORM queries against real data, writing postmortems with concrete numbers.

optional_mcps.name: filesystem
optional_mcps.description: Read/write/search files and directories on the local filesystem, with allowlist of permitted paths. Useful when the agent needs to operate outside the project root (e.g. /tmp, a sibling monorepo, a shared docs dir).

FILESYSTEM_ALLOWED_DIRS.description: Comma-separated absolute paths the MCP is allowed to touch. Default: the current working directory. Example: /home/me/projects,/tmp/mcp-scratch. Server refuses paths outside this list.

optional_mcps.use_when: Reading config from a sibling repo, batch-renaming files, searching across multiple project roots, working with /tmp scratch dirs that opencode's built-in tools don't reach.

optional_mcps.name: sentry
optional_mcps.description: Query Sentry for unresolved issues, error frequency, stack traces, and recent events. Triage production incidents without leaving the agent.

SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN.description: Sentry auth token. Generate at https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/. Needs 'event:read', 'project:read', 'org:read' scopes.

optional_mcps.use_when: Production incident response, finding regression-causing issues, getting stack traces for incident postmortems, checking error rates before a deploy.

optional_mcps.name: linear
optional_mcps.description: Read and update Linear issues, projects, cycles, and teams. Useful for agents that need to track work alongside the user (creating follow-up issues from PR review, updating ticket status, fetching acceptance criteria).

LINEAR_API_KEY.description: Linear personal API key. Generate at https://linear.app/settings/api. Needs 'read' and 'write' scopes for full functionality.

optional_mcps.use_when: Auto-creating Linear tickets from /pr-review findings, fetching acceptance criteria before implementing, updating ticket status after merging, cross-referencing PRs to tickets.

optional_mcps.name: notion
optional_mcps.description: Read and search Notion pages, databases, and blocks. Useful for grounding the agent in team docs, design specs, runbooks, or product requirements.

NOTION_API_KEY.description: Notion internal integration token. Create at https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations. The integration must be explicitly shared with the pages/databases you want to query.

optional_mcps.use_when: Reading product specs from Notion before implementing, searching runbooks during incident response, pulling design docs into a PRD, checking team conventions.

optional_mcps.name: slack
optional_mcps.description: Read Slack channels, threads, and direct messages. Post messages on behalf of the user. Useful for triaging notifications, searching history, and posting incident updates.

SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.description: Slack bot token (xoxb-...) OR user token (xoxp-...). Create at https://api.slack.com/apps. Bot token needs 'channels:history', 'channels:read', 'chat:write', 'users:read' scopes for the demo workflow.

optional_mcps.use_when: Triaging unread Slack messages, posting incident updates to a channel, searching past decisions in threads, summarizing long discussions.

optional_mcps.name: brave-search
optional_mcps.description: Web search via Brave. Useful for up-to-date information that isn't in the agent's training data (recent CVEs, latest library versions, breaking changes, current best practices).

BRAVE_API_KEY.description: Brave Search API key. Free tier (2000 queries/month) at https://brave.com/search/api/. Sufficient for most agent usage.

optional_mcps.use_when: Looking up recent CVEs, verifying library versions before recommending, finding breaking changes in upstream APIs, fact-checking training-data claims about recent events.

optional_mcps.name: fetch
optional_mcps.description: Fetch any URL and return its content as markdown. Generic HTTP fetcher with HTML-to-markdown conversion. Useful for reading arbitrary web pages, API docs not in Context7, blog posts, RFCs.
optional_mcps.use_when: Reading docs that Context7 doesn't have, fetching RFCs or specifications, pulling blog posts the user references, scraping GitHub raw files (use github MCP first if available).

optional_mcps.name: gitlab
optional_mcps.description: Read GitLab issues, MRs, code search, project metadata. Same shape as the GitHub MCP but for self-hosted or gitlab.com projects. Useful for teams on GitLab instead of GitHub.

GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.description: GitLab personal access token. Generate at https://gitlab.com/-/user_settings/personal_access_tokens (or your self-hosted /-/user_settings/personal_access_tokens). Needs 'api' and 'read_repository' scopes.

GITLAB_HOST.description: GitLab host URL. Default 'https://gitlab.com'. For self-hosted: 'https://gitlab.yourcompany.com'.

optional_mcps.use_when: Working on a GitLab-hosted project, fetching MRs for review, searching code across a GitLab org, releasing from a GitLab CI pipeline.

optional_mcps.name: supabase
optional_mcps.description: Query and manage a Supabase project: list tables, run SQL, inspect schema, read auth users and storage objects. Requires a Supabase access token.

SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN.description: Supabase access token. Create one at https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens. Lets the agent read schema and run queries against your projects.

optional_mcps.use_when: Debugging a Supabase backend, inspecting tables or RLS policies, validating migrations, checking auth or storage data during development.

optional_mcps.name: vercel
optional_mcps.description: Manage Vercel projects, deployments, domains and environment variables from the agent. Requires a Vercel access token.

VERCEL_TOKEN.description: Vercel access token. Create one at https://vercel.com/account/tokens. Scope decides whether the agent can read or also mutate deployments.

optional_mcps.use_when: Checking deployment status after a push, reading build logs from a failed deploy, listing environment variables, promoting or rolling back a release.

optional_mcps.name: stripe
optional_mcps.description: Read Stripe customers, subscriptions, invoices, payments and events. Requires a Stripe secret key.

STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.description: Stripe secret key (sk_...). Prefer a TEST-mode key unless there is a specific reason not to. Create one at https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/apikeys.

optional_mcps.use_when: Debugging a failed payment, inspecting a subscription state, correlating webhooks with app data, verifying what a customer was actually charged.
